skill.name: xlsx
skill.description: Create, edit, analyze, and validate spreadsheet files, including XLSX, CSV, and TSV. The skill provides pandas and openpyxl workflows, financial model formatting rules, and LibreOffice formula recalculation guidance.
skill.summary: Create, edit, analyze, and validate Excel workbooks with formulas and formatting.
skill.author: Azeem-2

security_audit.summary: The Python helper uses fixed local subprocess calls for LibreOffice and gtimeout without shell interpolation, so direct command injection evidence is limited. It writes and executes a persistent LibreOffice macro in a hidden user profile, and it trusts an existing macro by function name. Most Markdown findings are false positives from code fences or inline spreadsheet examples, and no prompt injection text was found.

remediation.issue: Persistent LibreOffice macro installation in the user profile
remediation.suggestion: Use an isolated temporary LibreOffice user profile, or ask for explicit confirmation before writing macro files under the user profile.

remediation.issue: Existing LibreOffice macro is trusted by function name only
remediation.suggestion: Verify the macro file contents exactly before reuse, or replace it only after clear user approval.

remediation.issue: External office binary execution is required for recalculation
remediation.suggestion: Resolve a trusted soffice path, keep shell execution disabled, and show the command before running it.

remediation.issue: Command examples are mixed with mandatory workflow steps
remediation.suggestion: Separate examples from required execution steps and include a consent step before running recalc.py.

semantic_findings.title: Existing LibreOffice Macro Trusted By Name
semantic_findings.description: recalc.py accepts an existing Module1.xba if it contains RecalculateAndSave, then executes the application macro URL. A modified or preexisting macro with that function name could run during recalculation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code checks only for the function name before reusing the macro file and later invokes that named application macro. The behavior is clear, though exploitation depends on prior local macro modification.

content.value_statement: Spreadsheet automation often breaks formulas, formatting, or source assumptions. This skill guides Claude and Codex through Excel creation, editing, analysis, and formula checks.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of XLSX workbooks with formulas, formatting, sheets, and comments.
Uses pandas patterns for reading, summarizing, and exporting spreadsheet data.
Uses openpyxl patterns for preserving and editing existing workbook structure.
Provides financial model formatting rules for assumptions, formulas, links, and units.
Includes recalc.py to recalculate formulas with LibreOffice and report Excel errors.
Explains validation checks for references, edge cases, and formula error types.
limitations: Requires Python libraries such as pandas and openpyxl in the execution environment.
Formula recalculation depends on LibreOffice and may modify the user LibreOffice macro profile.
It does not replace human review for financial assumptions, model logic, or source accuracy.
Large or complex workbooks may need additional runtime and targeted sheet processing.

use_cases.title: Prepare Operational Reports
use_cases.description: Create formatted workbooks with clean tables, totals, and formulas from raw exports.

use_cases.title: Review Financial Models
use_cases.description: Apply formatting standards, preserve formulas, and check workbooks for common formula errors.

use_cases.title: Analyze Spreadsheet Data
use_cases.description: Read multi-sheet files, summarize columns, and export analysis results into a new workbook.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Workbook
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a workbook from this table. Add clear headers, totals, simple formatting, and save it as an XLSX file.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize Spreadsheet Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Read this workbook, summarize each sheet, identify missing values, and create a clean summary workbook.

prompt_templates.title: Update an Existing Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Update this workbook with the new assumptions. Preserve existing formulas, formatting, sheet names, and source notes.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Validated Financial Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a financial model with separate assumptions, linked formulas, source notes, formatting standards, and formula validation results.

output_examples.input: Create a monthly expense tracker with categories, totals, and a summary sheet.
output_examples.output: An XLSX workbook with an expense input sheet, monthly totals, category summaries, and formatted headers.

output_examples.input: Analyze this sales workbook and highlight issues before board reporting.
output_examples.output: A reviewed workbook summary with sheet-level findings, missing data notes, formula error locations, and recommended fixes.

output_examples.input: Update a revenue model with new growth assumptions and preserve formulas.
output_examples.output: A revised workbook with updated assumption cells, linked forecast formulas, consistent formatting, and validation notes.

best_practices: Use formulas for calculated values so workbooks update when inputs change.
Preserve existing formatting and template conventions when editing user files.
Validate references, edge cases, and formula errors before delivering workbooks.
anti_patterns: Hardcoding calculated totals that should remain dynamic formulas.
Saving a formula workbook after loading only calculated values.
Changing established workbook formatting without a user request.

faq.question: What spreadsheet formats does this skill support?
faq.answer: It focuses on XLSX workflows and also discusses CSV, TSV, and related spreadsheet data files.

faq.question: Can it preserve formulas in existing workbooks?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance recommends openpyxl workflows that preserve formulas while editing workbook content.

faq.question: Does it calculate Excel formulas by itself?
faq.answer: No. It uses LibreOffice through recalc.py when formula recalculation is needed.

faq.question: Is it suitable for financial models?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes formatting, assumption placement, source note, and formula validation guidance for financial models.

faq.question: What should users verify before delivery?
faq.answer: Users should verify formulas, references, formatting, source assumptions, and any reported spreadsheet errors.

faq.question: Does the helper script change local settings?
faq.answer: Yes. The recalculation helper can create a LibreOffice macro file in the user profile.
